content.intro: This lesson covers VBA Security and Deployment as part of Macros and VBA Automation. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: VBA Security and Deployment contributes to reliable business reporting and professional spreadsheet delivery. Document assumptions, verify results independently, and separate optional platform tools from core Excel behavior. Compatibility: VBA macros require a macro-enabled workbook when they need to be saved with the file, and they are not supported in Excel for the web. Enable macros only for trusted files and review macro security settings.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: VBA Security and Deployment focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: Macro security; Trusted and signed code; Sharing .xlsm workbooks; Platform compatibility and the Excel VBA reference. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
items: Platform compatibility and the Excel VBA reference

content_blocks.code:
Sub AddReportTimestamp()
    Range("B1").Value = Now
End Sub
content_blocks.expected_output: Writes the current date/time into cell B1 in the active worksheet. Test on a copy of a workbook; the macro was not executed by CodeLeaf.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run only inside desktop Excel’s VBA editor on a non-sensitive copy of a workbook. Save as .xlsm only if the macro must be retained; use trusted code and inspect permissions.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a small, known dataset for vba security and deployment. Apply the example above, compute or inspect at least one result independently, then deliberately try a blank, duplicate, boundary, or not-found case where relevant.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates vba security and deployment. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

content.task: Build or inspect an Excel example that demonstrates vba security and deployment; use the example to verify one normal and one edge case, and write down any version or tool dependency.
task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.
The learner records an expected output and independently compares it with the actual result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
hints: Reduce the problem to a small range with known values before scaling it up.
Inspect cell values and formulas, not only displayed formatting; verify data types, references and range boundaries.
Compare expected versus actual results and check the Microsoft documentation for version-specific functions or tools.
content.expected_output: Writes the current date/time into cell B1 in the active worksheet. Test on a copy of a workbook; the macro was not executed by CodeLeaf.
common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
Using an incorrect range boundary, a mismatched lookup key, or an unverified assumption.
Trusting a result without comparing it with a known calculation or checking a failure/edge case.
